In trying to run Wallace (in R 4.1.2), the following warning comes up and prevents the application from opening in my browser:

"Warning: Error in shinythemes::shinytheme: united is not an available theme.
Valid themes are: .
82:stop
81: shinythemes::shinytheme"

Any advice? I have checked for updates, re-installed packages, etc.

Thanks,
Amy

messages.subject: possible error in base code (RMD issue)
messages.subject_clean: possible error in base code (RMD issue)
messages.body_plain:
Hi team,

    I'm currently using Wallace to build a repeatable study focused on mammals in the Northern Andes. I'm trying to use/modify the RMD for one species so I can automate running SDMs on multiple species. While re-running the RMD for one species, I ran into an issue where when the environmental df (occs_vals_Ap) and occurrence df (occs_Ap) had differing numbers of rows and therefore wouldn't cbind. After looking into this, I realized there was possibly an error in the base code when removing NA's from the extracted environmental values and the corresponding occurrence dataset.

The code is as follows:
# Create environmental object
## Specify the directory with the environmental variables
dir_envs_Ap <- "/Volumes/BETH'S DRIV/zarnetske_lab/CHELSA_4_only"
envs_path <- file.path(dir_envs_Ap, c('srtm_crop.tif', 'bio6_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio5_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio14_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio13_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif'))
# Create environmental object
envs_Ap <- envs_userEnvs(
  rasPath = envs_path,
  rasName = c('srtm_crop.tif', 'bio6_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio5_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio14_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif', 'bio13_1981.2010_V.2.1.tif'),
  doBrick = FALSE)
occs_xy_Ap <- occs_Ap[c('longitude', 'latitude')]
occs_vals_Ap <- as.data.frame(raster::extract(envs_Ap, occs_xy_Ap, cellnumbers = TRUE))
# Remove duplicated same cell values
occs_Ap <- occs_Ap[!duplicated(occs_vals_Ap[, 1]), ]
occs_vals_Ap <- occs_vals_Ap[!duplicated(occs_vals_Ap[, 1]), -1]
# remove occurrence records with NA environmental values
occs_Ap <- occs_Ap[!(rowSums(is.na <http://is.na>(occs_vals_Ap)) > 1), ] # where the issue starts
# also remove variable value rows with NA environmental values
occs_vals_Ap <- na.omit(occs_vals_Ap)
# add columns for env variable values for each occurrence record
occs_Ap <- cbind(occs_Ap, occs_vals_Ap) # this would throw an error saying that the row numbers were different

I realized the code should probably read:
occs_Ap_2 <- occs_Ap[!(rowSums(is.na <http://is.na>(occs_vals_Ap)) >= 1), ] # greater than or equal to

This way all rows with NA's are removed. Otherwise it's including NA's in the final dataset. After making this change, the code ran smoothly.

Just thought this would be an easy fix and worth mentioning.

Best,
Beth
